reference_capture.note: Freeze simulation time at the URL timestamp while exposure settles. URLs do not encode exposure or all rendering preferences.

scenes.name: bright-reflective-points
scenes.purpose: With bloom disabled, unresolved Mercury and Venus should receive the same brightness-dependent halo treatment as background stars in calibrated point styles, without changing physical exposure.

scenes.name: dusk
scenes.purpose: Atmospheric metering near sunset; check sky color and horizon clipping.

scenes.name: day-zenith
scenes.purpose: Daytime atmospheric light must be metered even without surface depth; sky should not wash out white.

scenes.name: night
scenes.purpose: Bounded dark adaptation should reveal stars without making unlit ground bright.

scenes.name: orientation-a
scenes.purpose: Compare settled exposure with orientation-b at the same observer position and time.

scenes.name: orientation-b
scenes.purpose: Compare settled exposure with orientation-a at the same observer position and time.

scenes.name: earth-overview
scenes.purpose: Black space around the resolved Earth must not drive exposure high enough to clip the planet.

scenes.name: earth-overview-wide
scenes.purpose: Derived from earth-overview with a 60-degree field of view; increasing black coverage should not wash out Earth.

scenes.name: sun-zenith
scenes.purpose: The resolved Sun should remain bright without duplicate daylight dimming or underexposing the surrounding sky.

scenes.name: earth-sun-transition-overview
scenes.purpose: Starting view for the small-Sun transition; Earth must remain correctly exposed.

scenes.name: earth-sun-transition-starfield
scenes.purpose: Near 1 AU, a visible Sun must lower exposure and suppress faint stars rather than being discarded as an outlier; verify convergence from both Earth and dark-sky views.

scenes.name: earth-sun-transition-clear-starfield
scenes.purpose: With the Sun outside the view, dark adaptation should recover the starfield independently of the preceding view; exposure need not match the Sun-containing view.
